newsitem.title: USA: Calpine buys stake in Enron power plants.
newsitem.headline: Calpine buys stake in Enron power plants.

text.p: Calpine Corp said Tuesday it purchased a 50 percent interest in two gas-fired power plants with a combined capacity of 827 megawatts from Enron Corp for $35.4 million.
In a separate agreement with the projects' lenders, Calpine said it purchased all outstanding non-recourse project debt totaling $155.6 million.
Calpine said it has assumed the operations and maintenance of the 450 megawatt Texas City Power Plant, located in Texas City, and the 377 megawatt Clear Lake Power Plant in Pasadena, Texas.

As announced in March, the company entered into a purchase agreement with Enron to acquire its interest in Enron/Dominion Cogen Corp, owner of the two gas-fired plants. Dominion Resources Inc owns the remaining 50 percent interest.

The acquisition of the power plants and outstanding project debt was financed with $125.0 million of non-recourse debt provided by The Bank of Nova Scotia and about $70.0 million of equity from Calpine.

Calpine also said it reached agreements designating two Calpine subsidiaries to exercise Edison International's rights to purchase United Utilities Plc's 50 percent interest in two power plants with a total capacity of 390 megawatts for about $40 million.
The two facilities, located in Florida and Virginia, are currently owned by partnerships comprised of affiliates of Edison Mission Energy and United Utilities.
As a result of these acquisitions, Calpine said it will increase its net ownership interest in power facilities to 1,582 megawatts.
